issues.failure_explanation: Finite dimensionality of $V\subseteq H$ does not imply $u_0\in V$ (e.g. $V$ a finite-element subspace and $u_0\in H\setminus V$). For such admissible data the scheme \eqref{eq:cnscheme} has no solution, since $u_\TT(0)\in V$ cannot equal $u_0\notin V$; hence Algorithm 1 and Theorem optimal_timestepping are ill-posed on part of their stated data scope. The needed hypothesis ($u_0$ already $V$-valued, or a projection with a data-error term) is assumed nowhere in Sections 2–3.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false implication by the standing hypothesis $u_0\in V$ (or initialize with a projection of $u_0$ and add the data error to the bounds, as done with $u_{0,h}=Q_hu_0$ in Section 4).
issues.overall_effect: The time-stepping scheme, Algorithm 1, and the main theorem are undefined/unsolvable for initial data $u_0\in H\setminus V$, which their stated assumptions allow.
issues.title: False claim that finite dimensionality of V implies u_0 in V; scheme unsolvable for u_0 in H\V
issues.why_classification: A single standard local assumption restores well-definedness; method, rates, and scope otherwise survive.

But $\eta_\TT$ contains $\partial_t f$ (undefined for general $f\in L^2$), so Algorithm 1's marking step may be undefined, and the proof identifies the error-based class \eqref{eq:approxclass} with the estimator-based one via Lemma reliability, which is invoked outside its hypothesis $f\in\SS^2(\TT;V^\star)$ — its efficiency part needs $f$ elementwise polynomial in time. The equivalence central to the optimality proof is thus unestablished for the theorem's stated data.

The source itself concedes the hypothesis mismatch and bridges it only by the unverified assertion that the cited proofs use nothing beyond the closure estimate and unspecified 'properties of binary refinement rules', which are 'all satisfied here'. No source-internal argument verifies the remaining refinement-dependent inputs of the optimality proof (e.g. overlay/admissibility properties of combined graded trisection meshes); the closure estimate of Lemma closure alone does not provide them.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the unique function that satisfies $\int_T \Psi_T v\,ds = v(t_{T+1})$ for all $v\in \PP^2(T)$
The constants $c_0$ and $c_1$ are independent of $u$, $\lambda$, and $\TT$.

issues.failure_explanation: For an invisible component $u_F|_T=c_Tq_T$ (normalized $q_T(t_T)=1$) one has $\|q_T\|_{L^2(T)}\simeq|T|^{1/2}$ uniformly in $\mu=\lambda|T|$ (as $\mu\to\infty$, $q_T\to 3s^2-4s+1$), so $\lambda\|u_F\|^2_{L^2(\II_i)}\simeq\lambda\sum_k|T_k||c_k|^2$; but the right-endpoint values are $|f_{T_k}(t_{k+1})|=|q_T(t_{T+1})||c_k|$ with $q_T(t_{T+1})=2(3-\mu)/(\mu^2+4\mu+6)\to0$ as $\mu\to\infty$ (and $=0$ at $\mu=3$, where $q_T(t)=(1-(t-t_T)/|T|)^2$). The displayed equivalence is false by an unbounded factor, and the recursion \eqref{eq:recursion}, which controls only right-endpoint values, cannot yield \eqref{eq:high_esti1}. The lemma's statement is in fact false: a pure invisible $u_F$ satisfies $\int_{\II_i}(\partial_t+\lambda)u_Fv\,dt=0$ for every $v\in\YY_{\II_i}$ (its residual has zero element mean and vanishes at $t_{T+1}$, i.e. is orthogonal to $\chi_T$ and $\Phi_T$), while $\|u_F\|^2_{\XX(\II_i)_\lambda}\gtrsim\lambda|T_0|\,|u(\II_i^-)|^2$, so constants independent of $u,\lambda,\TT$ cannot exist. The same obstruction falsifies Lemma infsup_lambda and breaks the proof of Theorem infsup: on a single-element mesh with $\lambda\tend\gg1$ the invisible $u$ with $u(0)=1$ has zero pairing with all of $\YY_\TT$ and $\|u\|^2_{\XX_\lambda}\simeq(2/15)\lambda\tend$, so the inf-sup constant degrades like $(\lambda\tend)^{-1/2}$; over eigenmodes this also defeats the dimension-independent constants claimed in Theorem optimal_timestepping. Additionally, the region decomposition permits 'small-step regions' containing no element with $|T|\lambda\leq\gamma_0$ (e.g. a mesh of at most $K$ large elements), to which Lemma infsup2_lambda's proof does not apply, and the same proof asserts the false bound $q_{T_0}(t_1)\leq1/(4\lambda|T_0|)$ (correct: $\lesssim2/(\lambda|T_0|)$).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must reprove per-eigenvalue stability with constants depending on $\lambda|T|$ — forfeiting λ-uniformity, the dimension-independent constants, and the quasi-orthogonality framework of [infsup] — or modify the test space/method so that invisible components on large-$\lambda|T|$ elements are controlled.
issues.overall_effect: The uniform (λ- and mesh-independent) inf-sup stability — the paper's central new ingredient — is false. The proofs of Lemmas infsup_lambda and infsup2_lambda (for regions without small elements), Theorem infsup, the Céa corollary, Lemmas nondegen and reliability, and Theorem optimal_timestepping collapse, and the claim that $C_{\rm opt}$ is independent of dim $V$ is unsupported; the MOR theorems inherit the failure.
issues.title: Inf-sup stability is false for large λ|T|: invisible ansatz components are uncontrollable
issues.why_classification: An explicit counterexample family (pure invisible functions with $\lambda|T|\to\infty$, exactly test-orthogonal with $\XX_\lambda$-norm growing like $\sqrt{\lambda|T|}$) shows the uniform constants cannot exist; every repair forfeits the central uniformity guarantee or changes the method, so no comparable version of the primary claim survives.

issues.failure_explanation: The key step bounds $\|\rho^{\rm (rb)}_R\|_{\XX^{\rm (rb)}_R}$ by a supremum over $\YY^{\rm (rb)}_R$, a space never defined, citing 'Lemma \ref{eq:infsup}' — but eq:infsup labels an equation inside Lemma infsupcont, not a lemma. Read as the discrete test space $\YY_\TT(V^{\rm (rb)}_R)$, the step is unjustified: no stated result gives inf-sup stability of continuous-in-time functions ($\rho^{\rm (rb)}_R=u^{\rm (rb)}_R-\mathsf P^{\rm (rb)}_Ru_h$ is not a time spline) against the discrete test space, and such a bound is false in general. Read as $L^2(0,\tend;V^{\rm (rb)}_R)$, the correct reference is Lemma infsupcont (applicable since $\rho^{\rm (rb)}_R(0)=0$). Moreover, the theorem measures $u_h-u^{\rm (rb)}_{R,\TT_\ell}$ and $u_h-\mathsf P^{\rm (rb)}_Ru_h$ in the $\XX^{\rm (rb)}_R$-norm although these functions are not $V^{\rm (rb)}_R$-valued, so the norms are ill-defined (the intended norm is $\XX_h$; the same notation recurs in Theorem fully_discrete_error).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define $\YY^{\rm (rb)}_R:=L^2(0,\tend;V^{\rm (rb)}_R)$, cite Lemma infsupcont for the inf-sup step (using $\rho^{\rm (rb)}_R(0)=0$), and replace the $\XX^{\rm (rb)}_R$-norms of non-$V^{\rm (rb)}_R$-valued functions by $\XX_h$-norms; the remaining algebra and the conclusion are unaffected.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem convergence_time_approx_V_rb_R — and through it Theorems exp_conv and fully_discrete_error — is not correctly established as written.
issues.title: MOR convergence theorem: undefined test space, mis-cited lemma, ill-defined norms
